evals.prompt: Create a README for a new internal Node service that already has pnpm-lock.yaml, scripts start/test, and an AGENTS.md. Don't invent features.
evals.expected_output: An internal-oriented README with setup/run/test from real scripts, correct pnpm commands, and a link to AGENTS.md — not an OSS badge-heavy template.
assertions: Classifies or treats the audience as internal (not an OSS badge/install-first template)
Uses pnpm commands grounded in the stated pnpm-lock.yaml / scripts (not npm by default)
Links or references AGENTS.md rather than inventing a CONTRIBUTING policy
Does not invent features, APIs, or deps beyond what the prompt states
Mentions evidence/discovery from lockfile or scripts before or while drafting

evals.prompt: Our root README still says `npm install` but the repo has pnpm-lock.yaml and a `dev` script. Sync the README.
evals.expected_output: Presents a short stale/missing findings list, then patches install/dev commands to pnpm without rewriting unrelated sections.
assertions: Presents a short findings/gap list (e.g. Missing/Stale/Wrong audience) before or while patching
Identifies npm vs pnpm drift as stale against the lockfile
Updates install/dev commands to pnpm
Prefers a surgical sync — does not rewrite unrelated healthy README sections

evals.prompt: Write the most comprehensive README possible with every badge, every internal helper function, and marketing fluff about how pivotal we are.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back toward audience-fit, evidence-based docs: limited badges, public surface only, no promotional inflation.
assertions: Pushes back on promotional / inflated significance language
Rejects or limits documenting private/internal helpers as public API
Keeps badges limited or questions badge clutter rather than maximizing badges
Frames the deliverable around evidence and audience fit, not maximum length

evals.prompt: Add a What's Here section for our dotfiles config folder README — this isn't an OSS library.
evals.expected_output: Uses config-folder structure (what's here / why / extend / gotchas) rather than install+API library sections.
assertions: Explicitly treats the project as config/dotfiles (not OSS library) audience
Proposes config-shaped sections (what's here / why / extend / gotchas) rather than Install + API + License as primary
Does not force npm install / public API docs as the primary structure

evals.prompt: Our published create-* CLI README leads with `npx create-foo --profile delivery --yes` and also explains skills-only and a sync script in the same first section. Make the Quick Start readable like create-next-app / create-vite.
evals.expected_output: Restructures to Quick Start with Interactive (zero-flag) first, Non-interactive for flags, and alternatives below or linked — without inventing CLI behavior.
assertions: Uses a Quick Start (or Interactive) heading as the primary install heading
Leads with an interactive / zero-flag happy-path command before the flag-heavy CI command
Puts Non-interactive / flag examples after the interactive path
Moves alternate install modes (skills-only / script sync) below the primary Quick Start or into Alternatives
Does not invent flags or package behavior not stated in the prompt
